annotations.title: Gyms, studios, courts and classes, and whether a visitor can get in

description: Verified East End places to train, 102 in all: gyms, yoga, pilates and barre, spin, boxing and HIIT, swimming, running groups, recovery rooms, tennis and pickleball courts, and dance schools. `access` says whether a visitor can buy one session: 18 of these are members-only, including Tracy Anderson Studio Water Mill, Tracy Anderson Studio Sag Harbor, 11937 Fitness, Equinox Hamptons, Gotham Gym, SLT East Hampton, SLT Southampton. `accessPolicy: not-published` means the studio sells class packs and publishes no single-class price; `classScheduleUrl` and `phone` are given instead. `reservationRequired` is set where booking ahead is required. Prices are quoted exactly as published, including seasonal pairs ($50 a class in summer, $35 off-season) and residency conditions ("Free (village residents + guests)"), with `pricingVerifiedAt`, the date the price was read, which is usually older than `lastVerified`. `doorsOpenState` / `doorsCloseAt` are computed on the East End's clock (America/New_York) and describe the venue's hours, not the class timetable, which is at `classScheduleUrl`. The `access` argument filters to one access kind; rows that fail the filter come back in `ruledOut` with the reason. `closed` names a studio the query matched that has shut for good. With no argument nothing is looked up and the answer lists the kinds and towns covered. Returns up to 8. `townScope` reports how the place argument was read; `townScope.recognized: false` means the name matched no East End place, the rows array is empty, and `didYouMean` lists near matches where any exist.

access.description: 'drop-in' = a visitor can buy one session; 'free' = no charge (public courts, the running group); 'no-booking' = you can turn up without reserving.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. 'yoga', 'gym', 'pickleball', 'spin', 'salsa class', 'cold plunge', or a studio's name.

town.description: A hamlet ('Montauk', 'Sag Harbor') or a region ('the Hamptons', 'North Fork'), in the asker's own words.
